story: At 1:17 on this humid, hazy Wednesday in Sumter Oaks, Gary is heading to Town Hall with a determined stride, while Donna waits patiently at his door with her pickleball bag, humming and checking her watch. Over at his porch, Hal is testing the sturdiness of his chair, content to carry it over to Rosa's, where she is optimistically arranging place cards and sketching a seating plan meant to mix up Hal, Gary, and Donna.
events: Donna waited: Standing at Gary's door with my pickleball bag, checking my watch and humming, giving him a few more minutes before we head to the court.
Hal (hal porch chair): Test the chair's legs and weight to see if it's sturdy enough to carry to Rosa's
Rosa (rosa dining table): Set out place cards and sketch the seating so Hal, Gary and Donna are mixed up

gary.thought_process: I've already looked over the parade rules and filled out the cart entry form, so the signup table has given me what it can. L-01 says exterior cart mods visible from the street need Architectural Review approval, so my lights and sound system can't just go on without a filing. Town Hall is right next to the square. Best next step is to walk over and get that approval started instead of loitering, so I can get the lights and speakers rigged well before the parade. L-03 means the sound system will have to stay off at night, which I can live with. It feels good to have a plan and be useful.

parameters.content: Heading to Town Hall to get my cart lights and sound system cleared with Architectural Review before the parade.

donna.thought_process: I've been standing at Gary's door waiting, and nobody's around. I'm at his house, not the court, so there's nothing to do but wait a bit longer or poke around his stuff, and rummaging through his toolbox or fridge would be rude. Gary's been good about keeping his word, so he's probably just running behind or out back. I'll keep holding my spot with the pickleball bag, keep my cheer up, and think about how to lock in doubles practice before Rosa's dinner Saturday.

parameters.content: Standing at Gary's door with my pickleball bag, checking my watch and humming, giving him a few more minutes before we head to the court.

hal.thought_process: Nobody's in sight and it's a hazy, humid afternoon. The complaints are settled, Gary and Donna kept their word, and Saturday at Rosa's is the thing left to do. I've already swept the street and gone through the notebook, so more of the same would be repeating myself. Sitting in the porch chair is the useful thing to do right now: it's the sturdiest one I own and I'm weighing whether it's the one to haul over to Rosa's. A good chair beats a fancy casserole.

parameters.content: Test the chair's legs and weight to see if it's sturdy enough to carry to Rosa's

rosa.thought_process: It's Wednesday afternoon and I'm alone at home. I've already blocked off Saturday, counted chairs, prepped crusts and the marinade, and written a grocery list. Gary, Hal, and Donna are all confirmed. Re-checking the schedule again would just be spinning my wheels. The one thing left is to actually finish the planning: the dining table is where I'll settle the seating and serving dishes so I know exactly what to buy and who sits next to whom, since I want Hal and Gary talking and Donna in the middle.

parameters.content: Set out place cards and sketch the seating so Hal, Gary and Donna are mixed up

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
